elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B expressly requires M&I to defend “Customer,” which is defined to include its Affiliates; Paragraph C extends those defense obligations.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B requires M&I to indemnify Customer, defined to include Affiliates, and expressly covers claims by third parties.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i) covers third-party claims that the Services or M&I software infringe U.S. patents, copyrights, or trademarks.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph C(i) extends M&I’s indemnity and defense obligations to M&I’s violation of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Paragraph C(ii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer data caused by M&I.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Paragraph C(iii) expressly covers M&I’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 requires the indemnitee to give notice of a covered third-party claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 entitles the indemnifying party to assume control of the defense with reasonably satisfactory counsel.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 requires the indemnitee to cooperate fully and assist in all reasonable respects.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph A limits Customer’s substantive indemnity triggers to Customer-provided content, data, or materials and Customer’s violation of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Paragraph B(i) indemnifies Customer against third-party claims that Services or M&I software infringe patents, copyrights, or trademarks.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears; the indemnity is broader than this permitted fallback exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: No Customer-combination exclusion appears; the indemnity is broader than this permitted fallback exclusion.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion appears; the indemnity is broader than this permitted fallback exclusion.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued use, modify, or replace an infringing item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy if other infringement remedies are unavailable.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No three-times-annual-fees super-cap is stated or incorporated in the rendered language.
